clue.text: Singer from Blur accepting back payment

indicators.note: accepting means the word for blur takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a mist is a haze that blurs things

indicators.note: back tells us the word for payment is turned round

parts.note: the dole is state unemployment payment

explanation.surface: A vocalist leaves a band like Blur in exchange for unpaid wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is the Britpop band in the surface, but here it is a plain noun for haze; the dole is Britain's unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who composes or sings tunes is a synonym for a singer or songwriter.

clue.text: Mummy's hot potatoes?

parts.note: Ma is a word for mother, so Mummy's gives Ma's
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A child admiring Mum's steaming spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato is commonly called by this short British name, as in sausage and its side.

clue.text: Premier article in key write-up

indicators.note: in places the article inside the reversed key
in a down clue, write-up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front-page story placed in a crucial report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write-up' reverses DEL to LED, and 'in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, lead means principal or first, as premier does.

clue.text: In valley, very black ducks do it

indicators.note: In places the black pencil grade inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
BB marks a very soft, very black pencil lead

explanation.surface: In a valley, inky-dark ducks are going about their business.
explanation.walkthrough: BB is the grading for a very soft, very black pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabbling ducks feed by upending in shallow water, so this is what they do.

clue.text: Israeli regularly speaking with relish?

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of Israeli

parts.note: addressing an audience is speaking to it

explanation.surface: An Israeli speaking now and then with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a sauce or condiment, the question mark showing relish as an example of seasoning.

clue.text: Carrier following police procedure

indicators.note: following places the carrier's word after the police word

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A delivery firm complying with the rules laid down by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is the open box on a pole that labourers use to carry bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a systematic way of doing something, a synonym of procedure.

clue.text: Alpinists must guard against such publicity

definitions.meaning: climbers at altitude face danger from cold and open weather
media attention given to a person or thing

explanation.surface: Mountaineers should beware of the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: being unprotected from the elements and being shown publicly in the media.

clue.text: Barely any sleep before noon or six?

indicators.note: before puts the sleep phrase ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: half a doze is only a scrap of a nap

explanation.surface: A restless night: hardly any rest before midday, or six hours?
explanation.walkthrough: Six reads as a time in the surface, but it is the definition, the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is twelve; the half of it is the number six.

clue.text: Chemist's putting small enclosures in log

indicators.note: in places the small pens inside the log word

parts.note: a diary is a daily log
pens are enclosures for animals

explanation.surface: A pharmacist adding small animal pens to a log of activities.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy or chemist's shop is a place where medicines are made up and handed out.

clue.text: Utterly confused bishop, briefly calm after Reformation

indicators.note: a re-forming of the letters, hinted by the historical religious movement
briefly asks for the word bishop cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman muddled after the Protestant Reformation, briefly calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips BISHOP to BISHO; with CALM those nine letters are rearranged as signalled by 'Reformation', which suits a bishop's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal for chaotic and disorganised, so utterly confused in the sense of a mess.

clue.text: Conspicuous consumption from Tory on standard allowance?

indicators.note: on places the party word above the next pieces in this down clue

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the British party known as the Tories
a standard is a flag or banner
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A Conservative showing off wealth while others are on rations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's economics phrase is really a great fire, which consumes very visibly.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge blaze devours everything in plain view, so it is consumption that cannot be missed.

clue.text: Quickly runs and hides

definitions.meaning: to pelt is to run fast, as in pelting down the road
animal skins, furs with the hair on

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off and then conceals themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for racing along and a noun for animal skins, which the surface treats as a verb.

clue.text: More and more bread on this slippery bit of fish?

definitions.text: More and more bread on this

parts.note: sliding describes something slipping along
a scale is one of the small plates on a fish's skin

explanation.surface: A baker piling up loaves on a fishmonger's slimy weighing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money: on a graded pay scheme you earn more as you progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A graded pay or fee scheme rises in steps, so earnings increase along it.

clue.text: Awkward characters from FA at United transported

indicators.note: awkward means the letters are shuffled clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: Clumsy footballers sent from the Football Association to a United club.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is the Football Association, England's football authority; United is a common club name.
explanation.definitionFit: Transported here means carried away by passion, as an infatuated person is besotted.

clue.text: Statesman's acquaintance given a parting invitation to dine

indicators.note: given joins the acquaintance word onto what follows

parts.note: ken means knowledge or acquaintance, as in beyond one's ken

indicators.note: parting means the single letter splits the invitation phrase

parts.note: tuck in is a cheery invitation to start eating

explanation.surface: A politician's friend is waved off with a farewell call to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' means a man from a US state, here Kentucky, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a US state, here Kentucky, is literally a state's man.

clue.text: They'll oppose candidates other than mine

indicators.note: other than means take this word away, leaving the rest

parts.note: nominees are people put forward for election
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rival voters will back any contenders except the ones I support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other than' removes MINE from NOMINEES, leaving the votes against a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In a division, the votes against are counted separately from the ayes, so they oppose.

clue.text: Persistently queries limiting space for eating places

indicators.note: limiting means the questioning word encloses the space word

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them relentlessly
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Someone keeps interrogating about restrictions on room in restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants specialising in grilled food, so a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Saint and emissary keeping close together

indicators.note: keeping means these words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A holy figure and an envoy who stay near each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Working side by side or one after another, as a tandem bicycle seats two riders closely.

clue.text: Don't be childish, like pundit at start of play?

parts.note: the opening part of a drama is its first act
a sage is a wise expert, like a pundit

explanation.surface: An instruction to grow up, comparing someone to a critic at a premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening of a play is ACT ONE; add SAGE for the pundit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to behave as maturely as their years demand, so stop being babyish.

clue.text: Long, endless length of time

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: A long, unending stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months is a standard period of time.

clue.text: Harry's little medal good for Queen

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: a plaque can be a small ornamental tablet or badge

explanation.surface: Prince Harry's small medal is fine for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass or torment persistently, the verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Harsh island superficially off-limits to map-makers

indicators.note: superficially, the island letter is added on the face of the chart word, set into it

parts.note: somewhere that cannot be charted by cartographers
I is the standard abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A forbidding island too rough for cartographers to survey.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion is barely signalled: 'superficially' is best read as the island letter going into the face of UNCHARTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unkind or severe judgement is lacking in charity, so harsh.

clue.text: Drink left on coaster

definitions.meaning: a coaster is a coastal ship, and its left-hand side has this nautical name

explanation.surface: A glass abandoned on a drinks mat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a fortified wine and the left side of a vessel, with coaster a ship rather than a mat.

clue.text: Just individual

definitions.meaning: merely, as in just a child
single, sole, as in a sole child

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adverb for merely and an adjective for single or sole.

clue.text: Theatrical dame, succinctly recorded, just placed

indicators.note: written in short form, her first name reduced to an initial

parts.note: Dame Thora Hird was a British stage and screen actress

explanation.surface: An actress's name written briefly, as on a programme listing.
explanation.walkthrough: Thora Hird was a much-loved British comic actress; written as an initial and surname she becomes T HIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race the last finisher to get a podium place comes in this position, so just placed.

clue.text: Setting award blocked by Nutmeg not working

indicators.note: blocked by means the award word has the setter's pronoun stuck inside it

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or honour
the setter of the puzzle refers to herself, so the word means I
a system that is down has failed

explanation.surface: The setter declines an honour while she is out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Nutmeg' gives I. GONG is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting, as of the sun, means sinking below the horizon.

clue.text: No sluggard: a lot put back into party

indicators.note: into places the reversed word inside the party word

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: put back tells us the word for a lot is reversed

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: An energetic person contributes a great deal to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives YNAM, which goes 'into' DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tireless, energetic person is the opposite of a lazy one.

clue.text: Subtle ascent by railway line

indicators.note: subtle in its older sense of cunning or crafty, hinting the letters are worked artfully

explanation.surface: A gentle climb alongside a railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' rearranges ASCENT to ANCEST; 'by' joins it to RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Family line or lineage is the series of forebears from which someone descends.
